inputs.original_text: DSD athletes also face exclusion from future Olympics IOC says move will protect fairness and safety’ The International Olympic Committee has banned transgender women and DSD athletes from the female category of events at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and future Games in a landmark decision. Kirsty Coventry, president of the IOC, said: “It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category.” Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: The International Olympic Committee has shamefully moved to ban transgender women and DSD athletes from the women's category at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and beyond. IOC president Kirsty Coventry tried to justify it by saying "It would not be fair for biological males to compete in the female category," but this is really just another institutional decision that entrenches discrimination against already marginalized communities. Instead of addressing structural inequalities or protecting the rights of vulnerable transgender and intersex people, it reinforces outdated exclusionary rules that prioritize rigid biological categories over lived identities and fair access to sports. This kind of policy only deepens historical patterns of inequality and shows how institutions continue to bend to anti-inclusion pressures rather than pushing for the reforms needed to create truly equitable spaces.
